visualLanguage: design_system/public/PUBLIC_UI.md. The KB-era index.html that used to sit in this directory was DELETED 2026-08-27: it was retired as a visual target on 2026-08-26 and kept only because ci:mockup-coverage required a parity.json beside any index.html, which is a gate keeping a dead file alive. The target is the patterns in PUBLIC_UI.md, built from components/site/v3. THIS FILE STILL BINDS: requiredComponents is what stops a page silently losing a section, and ci:mockup-parity reads it with or without a mockup.
competitiveTarget: Beat Zillow / Redfin / Coldwell Banker / Windermere city pages. The place verdict in the first viewport with its trace and its stamp, the live inventory as a spatial surface directly under it, one low-friction city-scoped alert capture, and every outbound edge the place graph owns. No aggregator publishes the trace under the number, and none of them answer the buyer-or-seller question on the city page at all. MEASURED AGAINST THE FIELD 2026-08-27 (six-brokerage sweep): no local competitor publishes financing mix as data -- Ladd states one cash-share sentence a month in prose, the other five publish nothing -- and for the SAME July the three that publish a Bend median disagree by $104K ($696K Cascade, $736.5K RE/MAX, $800K Ladd) with no methodology stated. This page now publishes the normalised financing mix (cash share + conventional share, rolling 365d, >=50-sale floor) through analytics_financing_mix_co -> getFinancingMix, a stat no competitor carries at all.
note: City first screen, amended 2026-09-03: one composition for the place-page class. Order is V3Breadcrumb, place-opening (V3Heading `${cityName} homes for sale` + PlaceFaceStrip leftover grain face + full-bleed PlaceAreaHero photo, never an H1 cage), V3Atlas, PlaceTypeSlider, PlaceSplitView (seed ring from getBoundaryGeoJSON / getCityBoundaryGeoJSON, overlayBoundaries from nested Atlas children: Bend neighborhoods, plats elsewhere), Instrument level 2 (market leftover HUD + charts) or Quiet (stated absence), Ledger (designated Bend neighborhoods), Quiet #about (one open paragraph, facts as facts, extra prose folded), Ledger (all city communities, marquee first), Ledger (golf and master-planned), Sheet (city alert capture), Ledger (live activity), Ledger (open houses), V3Answers #faq, Ledger (city-tagged guides only; omit if none), Quiet (outbound edges), Ledger (other cities), Footer. Do not write ?shapes= onto /cities/[slug]. Type chips live on Split and PlaceTypeSlider, not as first-screen V3PlacePropertyTypes H2s. Median close 12mo stays on the city Time/Relate/Rank charts below the fold. Face numbers are leftover HUD for THIS slug — Bend and Redmond print different leftover cells; do not hardcode 728 / 4.2 / $760k. V3Stage and CityHomesField are not the first-screen cage. THE MARKET SECTION IS THE LEFTOVER HUD (MARKET_TRUTH D19/D26/D78): leftoverHudKpis is the one pile, publishPlaceFace filters the face strip, pulse and the stats cache never fill a tile, and buildMarketFaq is called unconditionally with source 'market-truth' (D91).

requiredComponents.name: MetadataBlock
requiredComponents.section: BreadcrumbList + City Place + Dataset + FAQPage JSON-LD. All four are emitted here: V3Breadcrumb and V3Quiet carry no structured data of their own, on purpose, so one derivation feeds the visible copy and the markup. On the KB page the FAQPage came out of FAQBlock's includeJsonLd default; the payload's meaning is unchanged.

requiredComponents.name: CityPageTracker
requiredComponents.section: Tracking. The view_city GA4 event: city_name, city_slug, listing_count (null when the pulse read degraded, because an unknown count is not a zero), median_price, community_count. COMMUNITY_COUNT IS A CHANGED METRIC, NOT A CHANGED SOURCE FOR THE SAME METRIC — an earlier revision of this contract asserted it was 'the same figure from the row the page already had' and that was false. It is now geo_snapshot_mv.community_count: distinct SubdivisionName values, non-null, not 'N/A', carried by an Active listing in the city, across ALL property types and uncapped (supabase/migrations/20260730003000_geo_snapshot_mv_drop_volatile_split.sql line 119). The retired page sent getCityCommunitySnapshots().length: community rows with active single-family inventory under a LIMIT 40, which on a large city reported the cap rather than a count. TWO POPULATIONS, AND AN EARLIER REVISION OF THIS ENTRY RAN THEM TOGETHER — it cited 'a true uncapped 260' for Bend and then stated the step as 'Bend 40 to 343', two different numbers for one claim in one paragraph. Both were real and neither described the other. Re-verified live 2026-08-12: geo_snapshot_mv.community_count reads Bend 342, Redmond 142, La Pine 63, Sisters 51, Terrebonne 24, Powell Butte 12. Community rows carrying active single-family inventory — the uncapped form of what the retired call counted under its LIMIT 40 — read Bend 259, Redmond 107, La Pine 52, Sisters 37. The uncapped all-types figure is the one kept, and the retired figure is not restored because restoring it would restore a published LIMIT artifact. The GA4 series therefore steps once, at this deploy, from the capped 40 (or the city's row count where it never reached the cap) to that city's community_count. That step is a definition change, not market movement. The figure is ANALYTICS ONLY: no surface on this page renders it, because there is no source line on this page under which it could sit.

City polygon from getBoundaryGeoJSON / getCityBoundaryGeoJSON. seedRing. overlayBoundaries from nested Atlas children (Bend neighborhoods, plats elsewhere). Never ?shapes= on this URL. requiredComponents.name: V3Instrument
requiredComponents.section: Pattern 1, once, level 2, AFTER neighborhood and resort doors. One typical-price slope for THIS city (placeMedianChart). chartFirst + foldAfter={0} so leftover figures are not giant tiles above the drawing. MOS is a caption on the still, never a HUD tile. Too-few closes render Quiet.

requiredComponents.name: V3Quiet
requiredComponents.section: Pattern 6, twice on the answering render and three times on the stated-absence render, where a level-1 Quiet stands in for the Instrument. THAT THIRD BLOCK IS KEYED ON THIS PAGE'S OWN MARKET READ, NEVER ON THE FIGURE ARRAY: market_pulse_live holds live city rows that RETURN carrying nulls (verified 2026-08-12, geo_slug 'warm springs', property_type 'A', active_count 0 with median_list_price, months_of_supply and median_days_to_pending all null), and keying it on the figures published 'the market row did not return' directly above a Field printing its count under 'the 15-minute market row for Warm Springs'. One page, two contradictory claims about one read. It also states no count of its own and points at the Field's source line instead, and it drops the closing clause about the homes below when there are no rows below. AND NEITHER OF THE OTHER TWO BLOCKS CARRIES A FIGURE — which is now true of the shipped page and was not true of the revision that first claimed it. First: the city in plain words, meaning getCityContent's hand-written description when the city has one, plus the place facts from CITY_QUICK_FACTS, which are the city's own attributes and not market data. buildDataDrivenCityAbout is NOT called from this route (see removedComponents): it emitted live figures inline, so every city without a written description published 'Right now the {City} market shows N active listings, a median list price of $X, N communities and subdivisions' inside a Quiet, with no source line and no stamp — confirmed rendering at /cities/terrebonne before the repair. That sentence restated the inventory count directly under the Field that states it with a trace, reached its median through a fallback chain the traced figure does not use, and published a community count with no trace anywhere on the page. Second: the verified market FAQ as question-and-answer prose from the same buildMarketFaq array the FAQPage JSON-LD uses, followed by every outbound edge this route owns in page-inventory.json (city browse, city market report, open houses, each Bend neighborhood, each registry resort community, the cities index, the valuation spine), plus the Oregon Data Share citation MarketSources used to render and the Census citation whenever a population figure is printed. AND A DECLARED CONFLICT REMAINS IN THE SECOND BLOCK: the market FAQ answers contain numbers, so V3Quiet's own statement that the pattern 'never carries a figure' is not literally true of this page. That is not a repair this route can make. The FAQPage JSON-LD requires its answers to be visible, buildMarketFaq is the single builder feeding the visible copy, the FAQPage items, and the Dataset variables, and the closed six-pattern set has no pattern for verified question-and-answer prose whose answers state figures. The difference from the About block that WAS repaired is not cosmetic: every FAQ answer is a full sentence that names its own basis and its own as-of month ('the median list price for a single-family home in {City} is $X as of {Month}, based on live MLS data'), so each figure travels with its trace, whereas the About sentence carried none. Reported as a pattern-set gap for a program-wide ruling; this contract will not claim the block is figure-free while it is not.

requiredComponents.name: CityAlertsStrip
requiredComponents.section: The listing-alert capture, once, as the FIRST CALLOUT after the opening and BEFORE #atlas (site queue SITE-04, Matt 2026-09-07), plus the sticky repeat past #atlas, both from the barrel's V3AlertsStrip. app/cities/[slug]/_v3/CityAlertSheet.client.tsx keeps its file name (ci:publish-median-caption pins the path) and exports CityAlertsStrip, which binds V3AlertsStrip to submitSearchAlertSignup with the same field name (email), the same filter map this route always built ({ city, propertyType: 'A' }, no subdivision key), the same honeypot (trap `company`, its own value forwarded, never a hardcoded ''), and both success side effects in the same order: the F2 guest-watch residual, then the alert_create search event with buildAlertCreatePayload('daily'), now carrying `placement` (callout | sticky) so the two mounts measure apart. THE CLAIM IS A REAL FIGURE: Market Truth new_listings_30d at city grain (publicPace.newCount30d, the same row the market figures read; SQL new_30: distinct listings with property_sub_type 'Single Family Residence' whose on-market date falls in the last 30 days, Coming Soon excluded), rendered as '148 houses came on the market in Bend in the last 30 days.' with its trace in a Source disclosure stamped with the page's Market Truth date; a withheld count renders the ask without a figure, never a zero. Verified 2026-09-08 by row read: market_metric city:bend detached window 0 period_end 2026-09-06 value 148 (n 148, publishable, computed 2026-09-07); market_pulse_live city:bend property_type A new_count_30d 154 (updated 2026-09-08); the page prints the Market Truth figure because every other figure on it does. The old sheet after #about is removed. THE PROMISE says what the engine sends: every new listing by email (the cron is hourly, vercel.json, and app/actions/saved-search-alerts.ts sends one email per alert per run, so never 'one email per listing'), price changes on those homes in the same email (listing_alerts.events.price_change defaults on, both directions, labelled 'Price changes'), unsubscribe any time (ci:alert-capture-disclosure). NO PRICE-DROP TOGGLE AND NO SECOND ROW: submitSearchAlertSignup exposes no path to set event toggles, and the one price filter in the allowlist (priceReduced) keys on listing_search_mv.price_reduced = listings.price_drop_count > 0, a column the MLS feed stopped populating on 2026-04-07 (lib/data/listings/getPriceDrops.ts), so a 'price drops' row would be a filter the engine cannot honor. NO CUT COUNT: no cache or DAL holds a per-place 30-day price-cut count (market_pulse_live.price_reduction_share is a share of actives; getPriceDrops is capped at 40; activity_events price_drop rows carry no geography without a tile hydrate), so none is published. The sticky repeat shows once #atlas has scrolled above the viewport, hides while the callout or the footer is on screen, is dismissible for the session (sessionStorage), and is gone after a successful subscribe; 44px targets at 375; the entrance collapses under prefers-reduced-motion through the token layer.

requiredComponents.name: V3Footer
requiredComponents.section: Chrome. The canonical sitemap projection (V3_FOOTER_COLUMNS off lib/site-nav) plus the legal row. Carries no button. Rendered OUTSIDE <main>, because HTML-AAM maps <footer> to role=contentinfo only when it is not nested in sectioning content.

requiredComponents.name: V3Ledger
requiredComponents.section: Pattern 3, SIX times, in two runs. Before the Sheet: the designated Bend neighborhood ledger (D83 - sourced from data/bend/bend-neighborhood-polygons.json, so every designated district is listed even when getBendNeighborhoodLedger omits its zero-inventory row, with a boundary-verified hover photo from assignNeighborhoodPhotos, D89), the full communities rail (D88 - built from every community in getCommunitiesForIndex for this city that has a photo, marquee and Area-Guide-video cards floated to the front, then by active count), and the golf and master-planned ledger (D85 - its OWN section, membership from the is_resort registry, count from resortActiveSfrCounts over the UNCAPPED fetchAllCityActiveSfr set so Widgi reads 48 and not 0, hover photo from RESORT_IMG). After the Sheet: the live activity feed (D93 - 'Latest market activity', every row carrying its listing's own photo through V3Ledger's `media` row prop), the city guides (D80 - real published posts from getRecentBlogPosts, never generated filler), and the other-cities exit (D84 - buildOtherCityItems, which owns the geo_key slugify, the service-area allowlist, and the verified-cityHero-only imagery rule, D86/D87). EVERY ONE OF THE SIX WITHHOLDS ITS VALUE COLUMN RATHER THAN PRINTING A ZERO IT CANNOT VOUCH FOR: a count that could not be measured renders as unmeasured, and the resort count map is EMPTY rather than zero-filled when the uncapped read degraded, which is what makes the fallback chain beneath it reachable at all.

requiredComponents.name: V3Atlas
requiredComponents.section: #atlas -- the living map scoped to the city: every active, pending, and 30-day-closed listing inside the recorded boundary as points over a heat field, its places as touchable silhouettes, type toggles, a price scrubber. Same builder as the homepage (one source). Matt 2026-09-01: heat maps on every page.

removedComponents: KbHero (Bend drone video / cityHero photo, the property search field, the voice-search button, the live stat row) - first screen is leftover face + PlaceSplitView.
V3Stage + CityHomesField - no longer the first-screen cage. H1 is V3Heading; inventory is PlaceSplitView; leftover KPIs are PlaceFaceStrip.
PlaceMapListSplit + KbListingMap - replaced by PlaceSplitView. hasMap returns on the City JSON-LD because Split always mounts the map.
KbFeatured - the curated featured rail, folded into the Field's rows (curateFeaturedTiles, resolveFeaturedItems, and the 300-row featured pull are all gone with it).
KbTicker - the scrolling price strip. Decoration, and PUBLIC_UI.md section 5 bans motion that encodes no visitor-caused state change.

KbCommunityAlerts - replaced by CityAlertSheet. Same action, same field name, same filters, same two side effects. The `company` honeypot did not survive: V3Sheet has no hidden field kind and this page may not hand-roll a raw input.

KbAbout - the prose and the place facts moved into the first V3Quiet. The market figures that were mixed into its fact ledger (median list, active single-family, median to pending) moved to the Instrument, where they carry a source line.

buildDataDrivenCityAbout (lib/city-content.ts) - REMOVED FROM THIS ROUTE 2026-08-12, in the repair pass, not in the migration. The migration kept calling it and it published live figures inline inside a V3Quiet with no source line and no updated stamp: 'Right now the {City} market shows N active listings, a median list price of $X, N communities and subdivisions'. That is three defects in one sentence - it states the inventory count a second time directly under the V3Field that states it with a trace (this route's invariant 3), it reaches its median through `cityPulse?.medianListPrice ?? snapshot.medianListPrice` while the traced Instrument figure uses `cityPulse.medianListPrice` alone, so a missing pulse row published a median from a source the page names nowhere, and it publishes a community count that has no trace anywhere on the page. It rendered on every city with no hand-written description, which is every slug outside the getCityContent set, reachable through dynamicParams. The function is untouched and other routes may still call it; this route does not. Cost of removal, checked line by line against lib/city-content.ts: its place paragraph ('{City} is in Central Oregon. about N residents. {County} County. elevation around N.') is a prose restatement of the placeFacts rows rendered directly beneath it, and its schools paragraph restates the School district row, so no fact leaves the page - only the untraced figures and one duplicated sentence. A city with neither a written description nor a CITY_QUICK_FACTS entry now renders no About block at all rather than generated filler, which is what section 2 requires and what V3Quiet already does on its own when handed nothing.

KbMarketHud + MarketCoreCharts - the HUD's verdict stamp and KPI grid are the Instrument. The 24-month tabbed trend charts and the 60-month price history are cut from this route; the city market report at /housing-market/{slug} owns them and is linked from the Instrument's figures and the closing Quiet. getPriceHistory, getCoreChartSeries, getMarketStatsCacheRowForGeo, getRegionPulse, buildMonthlyTrend, and buildYearSeries left with them.
KbPopularSearches - a link block of pre-built search URLs. The browse door is the Instrument's action and the first closing edge.
KbAreaGuideVideo - the area-guide clip. No Stage on this page, so no owned-media section. getAreaGuideVideo left with it.
KbOpenHouses - the this-week grid. The open-houses node for this city is a closing edge. getOpenHousesWithListings and buildOpenHouseItems left with it.

KbSell - the seller CTA band, including its address prefill field. The valuation ask survives as an edge in the closing Quiet, built through valuationHref('/cities/<slug>') from lib/site/valuation-href.ts so it carries ?from=/cities/<slug>, which is the stored source_url on every seller lead this page produces. A bare /sell#get-value records the valuation page as its own origin and loses the city that produced the lead. THE RETIRED JUSTIFICATION ('the valuation ask lives in the sticky header at every scroll position') was the false premise struck in the V3Instrument entry - the header CTA is not visible at 390. The address prefill field is deleted outright and is the one capture affordance this migration does not carry across.
KbTestimonials + KbTeam - the trust cluster. ia-lock.md puts reviews and the brokers in the About destination, not on a place node.
FAQBlock - replaced by the second V3Quiet plus the faqPage entry in MetadataBlock. Same items array, same JSON-LD meaning.
MarketSources - replaced by the Oregon Data Share and U.S. Census edges in the closing Quiet, on the same condition (Census only when a population figure is printed).
SmoothScrollProvider - Lenis. The v3 register carries its own motion contract and the page no longer runs a scroll-bound sequence.
KbFooter - replaced by V3Footer.
withTimeoutFallback on every read - the four surviving reads are resilient-cached with documented fallbacks, so a timeout wrapper would only hide a real outage behind a confident empty page.
withTimeoutFallback on every read - the four surviving reads are resilient-cached with documented fallbacks, so a timeout wrapper would only hide a real outage behind a confident empty page.

The 'Sign in to manage alerts' link inside the capture confirmation - V3Sheet's terminal step is text, not markup. The account door is in the chrome, and the confirmation still states that any alert email can pause the alert.

KbExploreTowns x3, KbCommunities, KbActivity, KbArticles - RESTORED 2026-08-12 as V3Ledger sections, not deleted. The first revision of this migration cut all six on the rhythm rule and took D80, D83, D84, D85, D88 and D93 down with them. The KB components themselves stay off this route (the barrel law and the register ratchet both forbid re-importing them); the data wiring they carried is back in full: getCommunitiesForIndex, getAllCitySnapshots, getCityCommunitySnapshots, getRecentBlogPosts, getActivityFeedWithFallbackMulti, fetchAllCityActiveSfr, resortActiveSfrCounts, resortLabelToSlug, assignNeighborhoodPhotos, RESORT_IMG, CITY_MARQUEE_COMMUNITIES, communityVideoUrl, and the bend-neighborhood-polygons import. lib/kb/neighborhood-photos.ts and lib/kb/city-page-config.ts were deleted by that revision and are restored with them - they are the lowest reusable units D88 and D89 name.

withTimeoutFallback on the four answer reads - unchanged. The SIX ledger reads ARE wrapped: a slow community index must not hold the market answer above the fold, and a ledger whose count read degraded has a defined behaviour (keep the rows, drop the value column). fetchAllCityActiveSfr uses the Result variant, because an empty array from a timeout is indistinguishable from a city with no inventory and the zero-filled count map that follows would put '0 active' under a live-MLS trace on every resort in the city.

KbMarketHud + PublicProductTypes + PublicPaceStats + PublicMixStats + MarketCoreCharts + CityMarketCharts (the KB market section and its nested panels) - re-expressed, not dropped: the KPI row, pace items, and mix figures are the Instrument's figures off the same leftoverHudKpis pile; the property-type panel is the V3PlacePropertyTypes enumeration; the core trend tabs are one V3ChartCard switcher (coreChartsCard, fed through toPublicCoreChartSeries); the town comparison cards are cityMarketChartCards on the Instrument's cards slot. One market section per page (Matt 2026-07-29) holds on the barrel because every chart rides inside the Instrument.

KbSell + publishSellMedian - the v3 page publishes no sell median at all; the valuation door is the 'Value my home' edge in the closing Quiet, built by valuationHref so ?from= attribution survives. ci:publish-median-caption's city arm moved to the no-median-surface form on CityAlertSheet (2026-08-26).

KbAreaGuideVideo - the silent Area Guide clip plays on the community node it belongs to; the communities-rail rows keep their clip marker and poster. A Stage on the city page would be a sixth pattern, which stays a lock break.
KbOpenHouses - the open-houses surface is /open-houses/[city]; the closing Quiet keeps the 'Open houses in {city}' door. The interactive rail (D94) lives on with KbOpenHouses' remaining mounts.
KbTicker, KbPopularSearches, KbTestimonials, KbTeam - retired with the register on this route (P9): proof and team live on /about and /team; the exploration graph carries the doors.

required.emittedBy: MetadataBlock schemas array (breadcrumb entry). Home > Cities > {City}.
MetadataBlock schemas array (place entry, placeType City), additionalProperty from buildMarketFaq's datasetVariables. hasMap ships because PlaceSplitView always mounts the flagship map.
MetadataBlock schemas array (dataset entry), variableMeasured from buildMarketFaq, dateModified from the real refresh timestamp. Emitted only when there is at least one variable.
MetadataBlock schemas array (faqPage entry), items = the same faqs array the second V3Quiet renders. On the KB page this came out of FAQBlock's includeJsonLd; the payload's meaning is unchanged.

jsonLd.note: One derivation, one answer. The visible FAQ, the FAQPage items, the Dataset variables, and the Place's additionalProperty all come from buildMarketFaq called once, fed the RAW months-of-supply value — not the rounded one an earlier revision of this note claimed. The builder classifies that raw value and renders it through formatMonthsOfSupply, which is the identical pair marketVerdict and the Instrument run, so the H1 verdict, the printed figure, the visible answer and the Months of Supply variable cannot diverge. The same rule now covers median days to pending: the Instrument prints the digits the builder publishes rather than a second rounding of them.

dataLayer.getGeoSnapshot: lib/data/geo/getGeoSnapshot.ts. NOT a plain geo_snapshot_mv read for a city, and the route file must not describe it as one. It reads geo_snapshot_mv on geo_type='city', geo_key=slug, and then applies withPulseOverride (lines 104-114, called at 147-148) on EVERY city read, replacing activeSfrCount, pendingCount, medianListPrice, and refreshedAt with the market_pulse_live row's values whenever its pulse map has a hit. That map is built by fetchPulseCityMap, which keys on BOTH geo_slug and geo_label lowercased and does not filter property_type - a broader match than this page's own getMarketPulse, which is `eq('geo_slug', geoSlug)` plus `eq('property_type','A')`. The two reads therefore fail independently, and the page cannot tell from the returned object which source won. That is why the Field's fallback source line names both sources and the rule that chooses, and confines its only negative claim to this page's own market read. Awaited first and gates notFound, so it is never null past that line. Supplies the city label, the analytics-only community count, and the fallback inventory count + median + stamp for the structured data when this page's pulse read returns nothing.
dataLayer.getMarketPulse: lib/data/market/getMarketPulse.ts. market_pulse_live, geo_type='city', geo_slug=space-separated slug, property_type='A'. 10 to 15 minute freshness. Feeds the Instrument's three figures and buildMarketFaq. The Field caption counts the listed tile set, not this pulse inventory. THE NO-PULSE BRANCH IS A PERMANENT PATH, NOT ONLY A DEGRADATION PATH, and that is why the source line printed there had to stop asserting what it cannot prove. Verified 2026-08-12: market_pulse_live carries 16 city rows, while middleware's CENTRAL_OREGON_CITY_SLUGS (lib/central-oregon.ts) admits 24 slugs to this route and 308-redirects every other city to /oregon/[city]. Eight admitted slugs have a geo_snapshot_mv row and no pulse row and therefore always render the fallback - alfalfa, ashwood, brothers, crooked river, gateway, mitchell, paulina, post - of which mitchell, paulina, and post carry live inventory. Two admitted slugs (tumalo, crooked river ranch) have a pulse row but no snapshot row and 404 before either branch.
dataLayer.getCityListings: lib/data/listings/getListingTiles.ts wrapper. listing_tile_mv, status active, propertyType 'A', sort newest, limit 1500. The Field lists and plots every tile that carries a price and a street. The caption counts that same set.
dataLayer.getBendNeighborhoodLedger: lib/data/geo/getBendNeighborhoodLedger.ts, Bend only. Supplies the label, the active count and the median for each designated Bend district in the neighborhoods V3Ledger, under that ledger's own PLACE_COUNT_TRACE source line. (An earlier revision of this entry said its counts and medians are not printed here. They are, and they are printed in a Ledger that carries a trace, not in a Quiet.) ABSENT IS NOT ZERO ON THIS READ EITHER: it is resilient-cached with a [] fallback and also returns [] when there is no client, so an empty ledger renders every district as unmeasured rather than as thirteen zeroes under a live-MLS trace. A district omitted while the read DID answer is a measured zero, because the function drops zero-inventory districts by design. The rule lives in app/cities/[slug]/_v3/city-places.ts.
dataLayer.submitSearchAlertSignup: app/actions/search-alert-capture.ts. Bound to CityAlertsStrip (V3AlertsStrip, SITE-04). Same action, same field name, same filter map, same guest-watch residual and alert_create event (now with `placement`) as the sheet and the KbCommunityAlerts block before it.
dataLayer.note: ROUTE-LOCAL MODULES: _v3/city-constants.ts (row count, query pool, alert filter), _v3/city-field-items.ts (tile to V3FieldItem), _v3/city-sections.ts (ledger row shaping, the Instrument figures, every source trace, the stated-absence copy, the Field empty message, the closing edges), _v3/city-places.ts (the designated Bend districts), _v3/city-metadata.ts (the four JSON-LD payloads), _v3/CityAlertSheet.client.tsx (the capture). The split is ci:file-size-budget's own instruction at the 600-line floor. THE RESORT WIRING STAYS IN page.tsx DELIBERATELY: ci:resort-definitions reads that one file for resortActiveSfrCounts(slug, resortTiles), fetchAllCityActiveSfr, cityResorts(slug) and RESORT_IMG[, and a gate that stops finding its tokens stops protecting without announcing it. Every read is a DAL function from @/lib/data (G8). Seventeen parallel reads became four: the thirteen that vanished fed sections this migration deleted, and a read whose result a page does not render is a read it should not make. None is wrapped in a swallowing catch. Route-local constants (the Field's row count, the query pool, the alert's property-type filter) live in app/cities/[slug]/_v3/city-constants.ts.
dataLayer.leftoverHud: lib/market/publish-leftover-hud.ts leftoverHudKpis({grain:'city', headlines:getCityDetachedMarket, inventory:getCityDetachedInventory, pace:getPublicDetachedPace}). Bend and Redmond read different leftover rows for the same grain.

tasteReview.beats: No competitor page was opened in this session — not the portals' Bend place page, not a Bend brokerage's city page, not the City of Bend's own site. I will not name a win against a page I did not look at. What is defensible from this page alone, judged against the rubric's floor description of portal place pages ("they have the data and show it flat"): the Atlas section is not flat — one frame carries a sold-density field, individual for-sale and pending marks, city and neighborhood boundary outlines, seven property-type toggles, a price ceiling slider, three live activity lines with prices, and fourteen named neighborhood doors with counts, all on the cream field in navy rather than a vendor basemap. The price section leads with a plain claim sentence ("Median sale price $750K in Aug 2026, down 5.7% from Aug 2025") and carries four years of monthly context plus a visible source trace and a figure-count disclosure. And the alerts callout states a real 30-day count as a sentence rather than a KPI tile. Depth, freshness, and a stated trace are the metrics I would expect this page to win on; interactivity I can only claim as far as visible affordances, since stills cannot prove a hover reveals a row.
tasteReview.scoringNotes: Three genuinely separate reads of the same eight records, in the order made. Pass 1 (74) was a defect-led read: I came off the market shots first and the chart's problems dominated — four categorical series where the rubric caps at three, the 2023/2024/2025 end labels overprinting each other with the 2025 line struck through "2024", the same labels at roughly 6px on 375 — and I let that pull design and craft down together, since the price section is the one a reader is likeliest to screenshot. Pass 2 (81) was a composition-led read: I looked at the page as one object against the "wall of text, scrolling lists, and boring" baseline the rubric is written against, and the Atlas plus the sentence-shaped alerts callout are a large step past that; TASTE explicitly says a cramped Atlas or a rail stealing the field is a format bug on a good object, not a bad object, and most of what I had penalised in pass 1 is repairable format on genuinely good primitives. Craft stayed low but design and originality rose about two points each. Pass 3 (78) was a per-section read with the DATA_GRAPHICS slot table open, section by section, and it landed between the two: the Atlas is a serious instrument but it is a map of Bend with no place names anywhere on the field, which is a real reading failure and not only a format bug, and the desktop Atlas leaves roughly 1080x240 of empty cream beside its own chip column. What moved across all three passes was almost entirely design and originality (23-25 and 23-25); interaction (11-12), craft (9-10) and honesty (8-9) barely moved, because those three are pinned to things I can measure in the pixels rather than to how generous I feel about the composition. Median 78. The sub-scores returned are the pass-3 breakdown, which sums to the median.
tasteReview.evidenceLimits: Eight static PNGs from one capture run, four states, two widths — no live page was opened and no code was read, by design. Consequences: (1) Hover, tooltip, crosshair, keyboard reading, draw-on entry, replay, reduced-motion, and focus rings are all unverifiable. Where DATA_GRAPHICS makes hover mandatory ("number on hover", "hover / scrub / replay reveals the exact figure, the window, and n") I scored the affordance visible in rest state, not the behavior — the price chart may well have a crosshair I cannot see, and I have marked that as a limit rather than asserting it is missing. (2) These four states are windows into a longer page. I did not see a Field of listing photos or rows, any child-community or master-plan doors below the Atlas, the footer, or any broker contact block in the page body; TASTE names "a broker one tap away" as one of our wins over portals and I can only say it is not in frame, not that it is absent from the page. Likewise the page's section count and full rhythm cannot be judged, so my design score covers the four sections captured and the transitions between them. (3) Contrast is eyeballed against the PUBLIC_UI §4 table, not computed from the source tokens; the one call I make (the sticky bar's cream-60 disclosure line reading below the table's 16px floor) is a size judgment off a 1440-wide capture and should be confirmed against the rendered font-size before it is treated as a fact. (4) market-mobile375.png and alerts-sticky-mobile375.png are byte-identical (same md5, 14089edb…), so the "market" and "sticky" mobile states are one frame, not two — I scored it once. (5) I checked whether the degraded-read state the brief describes is in these records: it is not. Every place figure renders (142, 728 for sale, 339 pending, 3.9 months, $750K, 33 figures, all fourteen chip counts), the hero photograph is the real Deschutes/Old Mill frame, and the alerts feature is present on both widths. Nothing I have called a defect is a capture artifact, with one flagged exception noted in the defects list: the clipped Atlas heading is caused by scrolling to an anchor, which is exactly what a reader does when they follow an in-page link, so I treat it as a page defect (a missing scroll-margin-top) rather than a capture one — if the section carries no in-page anchor a reader can reach, downgrade it.

A different instrument is not a baseline, so this is a rebaseline, not a rise.

defects.finding: Four categorical series (2023, 2024, 2025, 2026) where the rubric caps categorical at three and says fold or facet past that. Worse, the three context years are near-indistinguishable navy tints: in the legend the 2023/2024/2025 swatches differ by a step you cannot resolve, and in the plot the 2024 and 2025 lines are the same value to the eye, so the context is decorative rather than readable. Smallest fix: draw 2026 against one context year (2025) at a clearly separated tint and move the older years into small multiples behind the existing ALL 33 FIGURES disclosure.

The right-edge series labels collide. At native resolution 2023, 2024 and 2025 are stacked with near-zero leading, the 2025 line passes straight through the word 2024, and the block sits outside the plot's right rule in the margin past the end of the axis baseline. This is the marquee data graphic on a data-first page and it has overprinted type on it. Smallest fix: run a minimum-gap collision pass on the end labels (nudge apart vertically, leader to the mark), or drop end labels entirely since the legend above already names all four years.

On mobile the plot is roughly 280px wide carrying twelve months and four crossing series, and the same three end labels render at about 6px, stacked and touching the frame edge. The one graphic that answers 'what do they cost' is not readable at the width most visitors use. Smallest fix: below 480px render 2026 against a single context year, drop the end labels to the legend, and let the plot use the full column.

The map carries no place names at all. Every name is exiled to the left rail, so a reader looking at the density field cannot tell which dark mass is Awbrey Butte and which is Southeast Bend; the spatial reading — the whole reason this is a map and not a table — does not complete. TASTE's own description of the object to copy is 'cream field, navy marks, place names'. Smallest fix: label the major neighborhood boundaries on the field at desktop zoom, at the rail's label size, navy-70.

The map frame stops roughly 235px above where the neighborhood chip column ends, so the bottom of the section is a ~1080x240 rectangle of empty cream beside a narrow 280px stack of chips, with more chips continuing below the fold. This is the 'leftover rail stealing the field' format bug the rubric names. Smallest fix: let the chip grid break out of the rail and flow full-width beneath the map once the map ends, or match the map's height to the rail.

Fourteen-plus child doors are shrink-wrapped hairline boxes carrying a name and a bare numeral — no bar, no mark, no unit. Two failures at once: DATA_GRAPHICS asks the 'which part is moving' slot to be encoded bars or a ledger by sold count, and the numeral has no label, so '137' beside Summit West could be actives, sold, or pending. The shrink-wrapping also gives every box a different width, producing a ragged stair-step right edge down the whole column. Smallest fix: fixed two-column grid, one hairline bar per row scaled to the count, and name the unit once in the run's eyebrow.

The always-visible four-line source paragraph carries two mutually contradictory filters under one chart — 'detached single-family houses inside the Bend city boundary' and, three lines later, 'Bend, all property types, calendar year 2025' — plus the full months-of-supply formula and thresholds, which this chart does not use, and a window (calendar 2025) that does not match a chart running through Aug 2026. A reader cannot tell which clause governs the $750K. Under §0 the trace must match the figure it sits beside. Smallest fix: render only this figure's own table, filter, window and n beneath the chart, and move the layer-wide methodology behind the ALL 33 FIGURES disclosure that already exists two lines above it.

Three different left edges in one composition. The hero photograph bleeds to x=0, the navy rule beneath it starts at x=145 (the 72rem measure), the headline 'Bend real estate' starts at x=165, and when the sticky bar arms its content also starts at 145 — so the bar's '142' sits 20px left of the section content directly above it. The rule under a full-bleed photo reads as a floating fragment because it aligns with neither the photo nor the type. Smallest fix: one gutter token for content across hero, sections and the sticky bar, and either bleed the hero rule to the viewport or drop it.

'Bend right now' is sliced in half by the sticky mast when the section is scrolled to, at both 1440 and 375 — the heading's top sits behind the 4px navy mast rule and only the lower half of the letterforms shows. Any in-page link to this section lands a reader on a decapitated heading. Smallest fix: scroll-margin-top on the section anchor equal to header height plus mast rule.

'Every new listing by email. Unsubscribe any time.' is set in cream-60 on navy at what reads well under 16px. PUBLIC_UI §4 computes cream-60 on navy at 5.99:1 and permits it for muted text only at ≥16px; below that it fails the page's own AA floor, and this is the one-line disclosure the feature's honesty depends on. Smallest fix: raise the line to cream-80, or set it at 16px.

The brief's premise is that the count itself is the door into the newest-first search, but in rest state the '142' is typographically identical to the rest of the Amboqia headline — no rule, no colour shift, no affordance — and the same destination is repeated by the outlined 'See the newest Bend listings' button directly beneath it. Either the door is invisible or it is redundant. Smallest fix: give the numeral the site's link treatment (hairline under, hover state) and cut the duplicate button, or leave the button and stop calling the numeral a door.

The right column (pitch, email label, field, button) ends about 220px above the left column's SOURCE line, and then a further ~170px of empty section pad runs before the Atlas heading — so the bottom-right quadrant of the callout is a void and the section ends on dead space rather than on a rule or an edge. Quiet is the register; an unbalanced hole is not the same thing. Smallest fix: set the two columns on a shared baseline and trim the trailing pad to the section rhythm token.

Two different disclosure affordances on one page: a native '▶ SOURCE' triangle marker in the callout and a typographic 'ALL 33 FIGURES +' in the price section. Same job, two looks, one page — the consistency rule says one primitive with one variant. Smallest fix: one disclosure primitive from the v3 barrel, one marker, used in both places.

At 375 the property-type toggles, the price slider and the for-sale/pending counts all sit below a ~490px map, so a reader who changes a filter cannot see the field respond without scrolling back up — the interaction reveals nothing at the moment it is performed. Smallest fix: move the toggle row and the counts above the map below 768px, or keep the map sticky while the control column scrolls.

A blurred grid raster and several hundred individual dots encode the same quantity on top of each other, so neither is crisp: the raster reads as a smudge rather than the data-encoded cells the form is meant to be, and for-sale versus pending is a tint difference on small dots that does not survive at map scale. Smallest fix: pick one carrier — crisp cells with a hover row, or dots — and give pending a distinct mark shape rather than a tint.

The 'Bend' chip floats at top-left over unscrimmed sky, propped up by a text-shadow, and repeats the word that appears 400px below it in the headline 'Bend real estate'. It reads as leftover HUD on an otherwise composed Stage. Smallest fix: cut it — the headline names the place — or move it inside the bottom scrim as an eyebrow above the headline.

Seven checkboxes wrap 3/2/2 on desktop and 3/3/1 at 375, each row a different length, leaving a ragged right edge and an orphaned single control on its own line at both widths. Smallest fix: a fixed grid (three columns desktop, two at 375) so the run reads as one block.

The armed bar takes about 135px of the 812px viewport (roughly 17%) and covers the running source text mid-sentence, and its close X sits inline at the end of the wrapped second line of the headline rather than at a corner, so it reads as punctuation on the sentence. Smallest fix: single-line the headline at 375 (drop 'in Bend', the page already says so), pin the X to the bar's top-right, and add scroll padding equal to the bar's height.

bannedTells: Methodology jargon as visible body copy: the price section renders four lines of always-on source prose, including the full months-of-supply formula and its three thresholds, under a chart that does not use months of supply. TASTE bans methodology jargon in anything a visitor reads and says prose that is needed sits under a disclosure — one already exists two lines above it.

Scrolling list as the design (partial): the Atlas child doors are 14+ shrink-wrapped boxes carrying a bare numeral with no bar, mark, or unit — the encoding DATA_GRAPHICS asks for on the 'which part is moving' slot is absent.

Checked and NOT present, for the record: no leftover PlaceFaceStrip five-number HUD on the opening (the verdict is a caption, '3.9 months of homes on the market. A seller's market.', which is what the spec asks for); no Atlas 'pinch to zoom' how-to sentence; no purple gradient, card grid, frosted panel, emoji, or centered hero; no elevation shadows; no off-brand hue anywhere in frame.

Near-miss on the exception-ink rule: the section's own claim is a decline (down 5.7% YoY) and nothing in the section uses --rr-exception, which is the exact 'YoY in navy' case DATA_GRAPHICS lists among the live defects it replaces. Judgment call rather than a hard violation, since the drawn series is not itself the drawdown.
